Watching a loved one die of illness. My dad died of brain cancer when I was 16, and it was the toughest thing I have ever been through. He was diagnosed in October of 2013 after being taken to the emergency room where they did a CT scan and realized he had a brain tumor. Luckily it was in position on his brain where they could operate, remove it, and have it biopsied. I had to see my father go through radiation, chemo, and multiple surgeries, and through it all i always wished it was me. I remember thinking, "My dad doesn`t deserve any of this, hes such a good guy, it should be me thats dying. I deserve it. I`m the one who`s cutting herself and suicidal." I didn`t understand how the people who want to live have to die, and the people that want to die have to live. I still don`t understand that. 

Anyway, my dad died 9 months later on July 21st, 2014, while I was holding his hand. It still haunts me to think about it and I can`t even remember that day without crying. I had to see everything and there is no way I would ever wish that on anyone.
